summary: An excerpt from Kate Douglas Wiggin's novel (Book 11, part 129) set after a graduation ceremony. Rebecca, feeling unreal about her honors and the burden ahead, is comforted by news that Miranda's speech has returned and that Miss Sawyer, her aunt, is improving, though she remains paralyzed. Emma Jane offers to pack Rebecca's trunk, and Uncle Jerry Cobb talks with Adam Ladd about Rebecca's voice and appearance, while Jerry frets over her parents and visitors who compared poorly with her.
one_line: Rebecca, after graduation, receives mixed news about her aunt while Uncle Jerry Cobb and Adam Ladd discuss her singing and looks.
key_facts: Miranda has got her speech back, because Rebecca's aunt has sent a letter saying she is better.
Uncle Jerry says he will sit up tonight so Rebecca can stay at the brick house and have a good sleep.
Emma Jane offers to pack Rebecca's trunk and attend to all their room things.
Rebecca feels that the honors and happy excitement of the last two days are a transient condition, and that the burden and anxiety will soon loom again.
Rebecca longs to steal away into the woods with John, who has grown manly and handsome.
Adam Ladd asks uncle Jerry whether girls in Boston are as thick as blackberries like Rebecca.
Adam says Rebecca's voice made the others sound poor and thin.
Uncle Jerry says his mother scolds him for spoiling Rebecca, though his mother is not far behind in spoiling her.
Uncle Jerry says it made him sick to think of parents travelling miles to see their children graduate and then having to compare them with Rebecca.
Adam says he will drive Rebecca home, perhaps the next day, and will visit Riverboro.
Miss Sawyer is paralyzed and will never walk far again, according to the doctor's uncertain diagnosis, but she has not lost her speech.
Class members remind Rebecca not to be late for the picnic luncheon and to come early to the class party in the evening.
